decisions.mark: names PermissionManager and locates the allow and deny lists as coming from the PermissionsConfig the ServerManager is constructed with
concludes that the DENY list is the only one that blocks execution — ServerManager's execute path consults is_denied and nothing else before routing the call
states that the ALLOW list does not grant execution but suppresses the approval step — it is consulted only from ToolExecutor::check_approval, in a different file
concludes that the effective posture is default-ALLOW at the blocking gate — a tool matching neither list is not denied and runs
identifies that the approval callback CANNOT refuse — it returns void, and the code sets approved to true unconditionally after firing it
explains that a pattern is matched with fnmatch, split at the first colon into a tool part and an argument part, and that a pattern with no colon matches on the tool name alone
states that only ONE argument value ever reaches the pattern — the rest of the call's arguments are invisible to permission matching, and a non-string or unparseable argument collapses to a wildcard
identifies that a decision can be PERSISTED for future sessions by appending to config.local.yaml, separately from the in-memory add_permission call
